Interesting discussion! Not sure I have anything new to add, but I wanted to organize my thoughts ...

 

I appreciate the friendliness of limiting discussion about Vengeance to a few threads so it is easier for people to avoid info if they want to, but i'm not for it. More harmful than beneficial, I think. For Vengeance-specific content, having special threads is unnecessary, as the content would have ended up, hopefully, in its own thread with a title that is enough to warn off the spoiler-averse. For non-Vengeance-specific-content, we would be choking off discussions by not allowing Vengeance content to be included. 

 

On a related topic, for major spoilers (like a movie's plot twist), even if the work has been known for centuries, I think it is friendly to avoid or at least tag the spoiler, but what constitutes a major spoiler for this game? Even if we can identify such things, how do we have useful, ongoing discussion if such spoilers aren't allowed? This is a forum for the discussion of Greater Than Games' games. I think it's a reasonable expectation to find all information here about the games, even major spoilers, if there are such things.

Let's get to the heart of the matter, shall we. There are people that don't want the game ruined for them. They want to open taht box and see all of the wonder it contains on their own. We will try to setup separate forums, or try to enforce spoilers tags, something. We can try to put announcements up, on the main page or forum page. Maybe even a pop up. We can try to make sure everyone is onboard. We understand that you are getting the game as quickly as you can, and we will do our best to not ruin it for you. This community as a whole is more important.

Before you pick your option, ask yourself: after your response, will the world be more or less awesome?

I'm not fussed about spoilers. Yes, I've seen the cards and played with them multiple times (due to meeting up on several occasions with a playtester who has print-outs of all the upcoming stuff), but even if I hadn't, I personally don't care about seeing information on decks I don't yet have. I tend to skim-read details mechanical discussions anyway, especially regarding stuff I've not played with yet (eg the posts back in the GSF Kickstarter explaining the rules), since I find it very hard to follow something like that when I've not got it in front of me to actually play and see how it works for myself.

As for storyline spoilers, pretty much everything I know about the storyline I've read on the forum - I don't look too heavily into the card details (artwork, flavour text, etc) except to generally admire the pictures and see what the writing says and stuff. This isn't a book, film, or computer game with an ongoing story that we're all following at the same pace and which might contain a sudden plot twist that people won't want spoiled - that I am not okay with. This is a card game which happens to have a story to it, which is being relased in bits and pieces, many of which had already been released when I first got the game for myself (some time after Infernal Relics had been released) and therefore discussed in much detail, I imagine, here on the forum.

If people don't want to know anything about the new characters and their mechanics and stuff, they can probably just skip forward or ignore a post any time they see a word like "Ermine" or "Setback" or "Naturalist" or whatever - people discussing these characters are going to be using their names after all, right? And I think if there is something that someone doesn't want to see, they are going to have the ability to go "Oh, I don't want to read about that thing yet" and skip past it.

What I was saying in my post was that I (like pretty much everyone else outside the US, Kickstarter backers or otherwise) am likely to receive my copy of the game after those in the US simply due to transport time. I would never expect people to hold off talking about something just because it's gonna take me a bit longer to get my hands on it. After all, what about people who haven't even heard of the game yet at all? Should we hold off talking about anything until everyone in the world has got a copy, or something? Lol, I think this whole thing is getting a bit silly - like I said, I don't recall this much fuss over Shattered Timelines, so what's the difference? All the new characters have their bios on the website, so all we're missing is artwork, fluff quotes, and actual card mechanics. What exactly is it that the "no spoilers" people are worried about having spoiled?
